root_cause.text: The renesas_usb3 gadget driver's standard request handlers (GET_STATUS and SET/CLEAR_FEATURE) fail to validate the endpoint index extracted from the host-supplied wIndex field, allowing an out-of-bounds pointer dereference when the index exceeds the number of endpoints.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds checks such as `if (num >= usb3->num_usb3_eps) { stall = true; break; }` in `usb3_std_req_get_status` and `|| (num >= usb3->num_usb3_eps)` in `usb3_std_req_feature_endpoint` to validate the endpoint index before using it. The commit message confirms that the handlers "extract the endpoint number from the host-supplied wIndex without any sort of validation."

intent_record.intent_summary: Add bounds check to prevent out-of-bounds access when handling endpoint status request.
intent_record.what: Added a check for endpoint number (num) against the maximum number of USB3 endpoints (num_usb3_eps) before using it to access the endpoint array; if out of bounds, sets stall and breaks out of the case.
intent_record.how: Prevents out-of-bounds access to the usb3_ep array, causing a STALL response for invalid endpoint numbers instead of potentially accessing invalid memory.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add boundary check for endpoint number in feature endpoint handler to avoid out-of-bounds access on invalid endpoint index.
intent_record.what: Added an OR condition to the if statement to return true (stall) when the endpoint number (num) is greater than or equal to the total number of USB3 endpoints (num_usb3_eps).
intent_record.how: If a standard USB request for endpoint feature has an out-of-bounds endpoint number, the function now stalls instead of proceeding to access the endpoint structure, preventing potential invalid memory access.
